name: Two callings, one mission: Nursing and Service

content.text: The compassion of health care workers and priests in his community inspired Lawrence from a young age. He was drawn to how they gave their time and heart to help others. In 2012, he graduated with a diploma in nursing from Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) Machakos. He then worked for a year before joining the seminary for priesthood formation.

His early clinical work revealed a truth that shaped his future: patients often longed for more than medical treatment. Many yearned for spiritual comfort, hope, and moral support. That realisation convinced him that both vocations could work together to bring holistic healing.

For Lawrence, nursing and priesthood are not separate paths but one mission. "Faith can calm anxiety, and compassionate care can affirm the dignity God has given each person," he says. The two callings often meet in small but significant ways: a quiet prayer before surgery, a few words of hope to a family after medical care, or a compassionate presence at the bedside during moments of distress.

His time at SONAM EA has strengthened this integrated approach to care. The programme's emphasis on critical thinking, ethical practice, and patient-centred care has equipped him to serve with both competence and compassion. One memorable moment came during a clinical rotation when he cared for a patient who remained anxious despite treatment. At their request, he prayed with them and saw visible relief, a living example of nursing and ministry working hand in hand.

The journey has also taught him that care is as much about presence as it is about treatment. Whether in a hospital ward or a parish setting, Lawrence has learned that listening without rushing, showing genuine empathy, and honouring the individual's values can be as powerful as any medical intervention. This understanding has become a cornerstone of how he serves, shaping his belief that health must be addressed in both physical and spiritual dimensions.

Balancing two vocations is not without its challenges. Time constraints, the emotional demands of crisis situations, and the discipline required to maintain spiritual and academic focus all weigh heavily. Lawrence manages this through a structured schedule, consistent prayer, and the support of colleagues, mentors, and parishioners. Self-care is also a priority, as he knows he can only serve others well if he is physically, emotionally, and spiritually healthy.

Looking ahead, Lawrence envisions serving in spaces where physical and spiritual care meet, such as hospital chaplaincy, faith-based health programmes, and community health initiatives. He hopes to contribute to Africa's health sector reforms by advising on policies that ensure health care remains compassionate, ethical, and accessible to all.

To anyone who feels called to more than one path, Lawrence offers encouragement through his favourite scripture: "For nothing will be impossible with God" (Luke 1:37). It is a verse that, for him, captures the heart of his journey, a life devoted to service, bridging the worlds of nursing and ministry.

content.title: Two callings, one mission: Nursing and Service
content.author: Maxwel Anekea
content.description: For most people, choosing a career means following one path. For Lawrence Munyao, a student at the Aga Khan University School of Nursing and Midwifery, East Africa (SONAM EA), the journey has meant embracing two: nursing and priesthood, both rooted in a deep desire to serve. In May 2024, alongside his studies, he was ordained into the priesthood, marking a milestone in a calling that seeks to heal both body and soul.
